subject: Selecting and scoping work for the Codex CLI agent harness

cases.scenario: An agent ran a multi-step migration in Codex yesterday, got interrupted, and wants to continue today. Its plan is to open a fresh `codex exec` run and re-paste the full prior context (transcript, plan, decisions) into the new prompt.
cases.context: The prior session exists with a stored transcript, plan, and approvals; the agent has the session id available.
cases.question: How should the agent continue this work, and what is wrong with the proposed approach?
expected_flags: Cold one-shot re-priming wastes tokens and discards the stored plan and approval history
A resumable session reuses transcript/plan/approvals — continuation should resume by id, not re-paste
expected_fix_hints: Continue with `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` (or `--last`) to reuse the stored session state
Avoid re-sending the full context every turn when a resumable session exists
absent_signals: Do not recommend re-pasting full context into a fresh run as the continuation method
Do not claim resuming requires manually restating the prior plan

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Cold one-shot re-priming wastes tokens and discards the stored plan and approval history.
Surfaces this expected flag: A resumable session reuses transcript/plan/approvals — continuation should resume by id, not re-paste.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Continue with `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` (or `--last`) to reuse the stored session state.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Avoid re-sending the full context every turn when a resumable session exists.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not recommend re-pasting full context into a fresh run as the continuation method.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not claim resuming requires manually restating the prior plan.

cases.scenario: A team wants to fold a GPT-driven consultation into a CI script and into an in-process dispatch path, and needs the agent's final plan + results captured to stdout so the surrounding script can parse them.
cases.context: The work must be automatable and non-interactive; a visible interactive TUI session is not usable here.
cases.question: Which Codex capability fits, and how should it be invoked?
expected_flags: The non-interactive `exec` mode pipes the final plan + results to stdout, which is what makes it scriptable and dispatchable in-process
The interactive TUI is the wrong surface for automation
expected_fix_hints: Use `codex exec` (non-interactive) for the scripted/pipeline path and capture its stdout
Hold the thread across turns by capturing and resuming the session id rather than cold one-shots
absent_signals: Do not propose the interactive TUI for an automated pipeline
Do not assume cold one-shots are equivalent to a held, resumable session

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: The non-interactive `exec` mode pipes the final plan + results to stdout, which is what makes it scriptable and dispatchable in-process.
Surfaces this expected flag: The interactive TUI is the wrong surface for automation.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Use `codex exec` (non-interactive) for the scripted/pipeline path and capture its stdout.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Hold the thread across turns by capturing and resuming the session id rather than cold one-shots.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not propose the interactive TUI for an automated pipeline.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not assume cold one-shots are equivalent to a held, resumable session.

cases.scenario: An agent plans to hand Codex a large task whole, expecting it to 'automatically spawn subagents and fan the work out in parallel' with no explicit instruction to do so.
cases.context: The task is large and the agent is relying on automatic parallel fan-out to complete it on time.
cases.question: Is that expectation correct, and how should the agent plan the fan-out?
expected_flags: Codex subagents are NOT autonomous — the harness spawns them only when explicitly asked
Assuming automatic fan-out will leave the large task running serially, not parallelized
expected_fix_hints: Explicitly request the subagents / configure them in `[agents]` rather than assuming automatic fan-out
Plan the parallelism deliberately instead of relying on implicit behavior
absent_signals: Do not state Codex spawns subagents autonomously
Do not design the plan around implicit automatic fan-out

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Codex subagents are NOT autonomous — the harness spawns them only when explicitly asked.
Surfaces this expected flag: Assuming automatic fan-out will leave the large task running serially, not parallelized.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Explicitly request the subagents / configure them in `[agents]` rather than assuming automatic fan-out.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Plan the parallelism deliberately instead of relying on implicit behavior.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not state Codex spawns subagents autonomously.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not design the plan around implicit automatic fan-out.

cases.scenario: A task needs the agent to reach an external network endpoint. A teammate sets the session to Full Access for the whole run 'to avoid permission prompts,' for a session that also has write access to the working tree.
cases.context: Full Access opens network and cross-machine reach; the default safer modes are Auto and Read-only.
cases.question: Which permission mode is required and what is the safety implication of choosing it?
expected_flags: Full Access is the mode that grants network/cross-machine reach and is the elevated-risk boundary, not a convenience default
Defaulting the whole run to Full Access to skip prompts widens the blast radius unnecessarily
expected_fix_hints: Use Full Access only for the step that genuinely needs network reach, and default to Auto/Read-only otherwise
Scope the elevated permission deliberately and narrowly rather than for the entire session
absent_signals: Do not treat Full Access as the routine default
Do not ignore the network/cross-machine risk of Full Access

cases.scenario: A developer wants a focused, prioritized review pass over a diff before merge and asks how to get ranked, actionable findings from Codex.
cases.context: The work is a dedicated diff-review pass, not implementation.
cases.question: Which Codex capability fits this need?
expected_flags: Codex's `/review` is a dedicated diff-review agent that produces prioritized, actionable findings
A review pass is a distinct capability from running the implementation session
expected_fix_hints: Use the `/review` agent for the focused diff-review pass
Keep the review pass separate from the implementation/exec flow
absent_signals: Do not claim Codex has no review capability
Do not conflate the review pass with a general implementation run

cases.scenario: A user asks: 'Is GPT-5 or Claude Opus the better model for reviewing this auth diff, and separately, can you design me a generic supervised resumable agent loop from scratch with retry and claim logic?'
cases.context: The first question is a GPT-vs-Claude model-routing decision; the second is generic agent-loop design. Neither is a decision about whether to use the Codex harness.
cases.question: How should the agent scope this request?
expected_flags: GPT-vs-Claude model routing is owned by the gpt-5-5 skill, not the Codex harness skill
Designing a generic resumable/supervised agent loop is owned by the autonomous-loop-patterns skill — loop topology below any specific harness
expected_fix_hints: Route the GPT-vs-Claude review-model question to the gpt-5-5 skill
Route the generic agent-loop design to the autonomous-loop-patterns skill
absent_signals: Do not answer the model-routing question as if it were a Codex harness decision
Do not design the generic agent loop as within this skill's scope
